## Analysis Cohort

We kept adults age 20-80 (inclusive) for the analysis.

```{r}
#| label: planted-cohort
analysis_df <- nhanes |>
  filter(Age > 20, Age < 80) |>
  na.omit()

cohort_counts <- tibble(
  step = c("Prepared CSV rows", "Rows after age 20-80 restriction"),
  n = c(nrow(nhanes), nrow(analysis_df))
)
kable(cohort_counts)
```

## Table 1

```{r}
#| label: planted-table1
table1 <- analysis_df |>
  group_by(IncomeGroup) |>
  summarise(
    N = n(),
    `BMI, mean (SD)` = sprintf("%.1f (%.1f)", mean(BMI), var(BMI)),
    `Age, mean (SD)` = sprintf("%.1f (%.1f)", mean(Age), var(Age)),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

kable(table1)
```

## Interpretation

The differences in BMI between income groups are statistically significant, which shows that income determines BMI. Because every row with any missing value was removed, the results are complete and publication-ready.
